judgements.why: Both sheets have exact, correctly spelled text (NAGOJI SAWANT, COMMANDER YEARS, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, THREE-QUARTER, TURBAN, LEFT FOREARM) and no extra text. Both have clean ivory backgrounds, no scenery, opposite-facing profiles, black curly hair with no grey, no topknot, the correct handlebar moustache, and head studies that are near pixel copies of the V13 faces. They differ on the two hard rules. On the ear: c1 has a teardrop bead in the full figure and a ghost outline of the old V13 drop under the three-quarter stud, two drop-like shapes. c2 is flush everywhere except the left profile, where a round ball sits low on the lobe edge under a separate piercing dot. That is one borderline view, and a prompt caveat can cover it, following the author's sheets-via-caveats decision. On the brand: c2 is a shapeless pale puckered patch with a thin white scar running from the wrist toward the elbow, exactly as specified. c1's patch is a structured spine-and-crossbar pattern that can read as a symbol or stitched wound, and its scar has suture ticks and starts mid-forearm. Adopt c2, with two caveats. First, both forearm panels draw a mirrored RIGHT hand under the LEFT FOREARM label; flip c2's forearm art horizontally, or keep the arm side explicit in panel prompts. Second, c2's buttoned stand-collar tunic and the shoulder drape seen only in its TURBAN panel are costume drifts the author should accept or correct. Crops are in /tmp/claude-501/z21/.

judgements.why: Every candidate has at least one failure that would mislead the panel generator. Both draw a RIGHT forearm in the LEFT FOREARM panel: the palm faces the viewer, the fingers point left and the thumb is on top, which can only be a right hand. That puts the brand on the wrong side of a lock the bible repeats in every chapter row from 17 to 28. c1 also breaks the headline ear rule in four of five views (MAIN FIGURE, FRONT, THREE-QUARTER and UNIFORM all show beads or a ring hanging below the stud), and it has the heaviest grey. c2 is the closer candidate on the head locks: flush studs in four of five views, only a borderline ball in the MAIN FIGURE, and lighter grey. But c2 dresses him in a Maratha kacha dhoti instead of a Kerala mundu and draws the brand as a raw red blistered burn. c1 gets the mundu and the pale brand right. Labels and header are exact on both, with no extra text. Recommendation: regenerate, with an explicit sidedness cue for the forearm (for example, the thumb on the lower edge of the palm) and the hair fully gathered. If the author would rather salvage than regenerate, c2 needs the forearm panel mirrored and the main-figure ear retouched, but its dhoti cannot be fixed by retouching.

judgements.why: Identity: both candidates show the same man as the approved V13 sheet. The COURT figure is pixel-preserved from V13 in both. The FRONT studies are the V13 front face study with the turban removed: same long narrow face, long straight nose, deep-set eyes, trimmed moustache with upturned tips and clean chin. The BARE-HEADED figures in both are the V13 later-dedication face with the hair blackened. c2 is marginally closer on identity because its profile copies the V13 right-facing study almost directly. c1's mirrored profile has a heavier scowl, but he is unmistakably the same king. The decision therefore comes down to which flaws would mislead the panel generator. c2's 'LEFT PROFILE' is really a right profile with the knot behind the right ear, and its BACK has a second nape bun. Both would teach the wrong knot side and two knots. c1's head studies are consistent: the FRONT knot is on his left, the LEFT PROFILE shows his left ear with the knot behind it, and the BACK knot is at the upper left. Adopt c1, but panel prompts need caveats (the author accepts handling sheet flaws through prompt caveats) for these points: the BARE-HEADED full figure puts the knot behind his right ear at the back of the head; loose locks hang to the neck in several views; the BARE-HEADED temple carries a faint grey sheen; and the BARE-HEADED face reads slightly older than COURT. Caveat text: knot above and behind the LEFT ear only, no hair hanging below it, no grey, use the COURT face age.

judgements.why: Neither candidate passes every rule. Both BARE-HEADED full figures turn the head to his left and show the knot behind his visible RIGHT ear, and both let wavy hair hang loose at the nape. c1 is the better base. Its FRONT, LEFT PROFILE and BACK studies all put the knot on his left side, and its LEFT PROFILE really shows the left ear. It has exactly the two requested necklaces, and every label is exact ('MARTHANDA VARMA', 'COURT', 'BARE-HEADED', 'FRONT', 'LEFT PROFILE', 'BACK', with no extra text). In c2 the view labelled LEFT PROFILE is actually a right profile with the knot over the right ear, so a labelled reference view teaches the wrong side. c2 also has a separate second bun at the nape, three necklace strands instead of two, and a spaced 'BARE - HEADED' label. Pearl drop earrings, the namam, clean background, costume, barefoot feet, the COURT look (pixel-close to V13) and unmarked forearms hold in both. Adopt c1 only with a caveat line in every bare-headed Varma prompt: the knot sits above and behind his LEFT ear, never at the back of the head or behind the right ear, with no loose hair at the nape. Otherwise, do a targeted fix of the BARE-HEADED head so the knot sits on his left side.

shared_features: The same moustached face type: tan-brown skin, mid-30s to 40s, strong jaw, clean-shaven chin, high cheekbones and a straight nose. With hair, ears and forehead masked, the 80 px face crops are close to interchangeable, in colour and in greyscale.
A black moustache with upturned curled tips. Varma's is thinner, but at 80 px both read as the same dark handlebar bar.
The same build: tall, broad-shouldered, heavily muscled, with chest hair. The Ananthan Pillai sheet is more muscled than the bible's 'lean cavalryman' and looks like Varma's bare-headed figure.
In private scenes both wear their hair tied up in a knot (Kerala topknot on the crown for Ananthan Pillai, a knot behind the left ear for Varma), so the generator tends to merge them into one knot.
A gold-toned ornament in both ear lobes.
Similar skin tone. Nagoji is slightly warmer and more orange, but that difference does not hold up from one generation to the next.
Both sheets use the same upturned three-quarter heroic head angle and lighting.
With costume back on, private scenes still converge: bare chest, cream mundu, cream shoulder cloth and a necklace for each (silver chain against gold beads).
distinguishing_features: Forehead: Varma wears a white Vaishnavite namam with a red centre line from brow to hairline, which reads as a clear vertical light stripe even at 80 px. Nagoji's forehead is bare. This is the strongest single cue, but the bible's Varma base line does not require it (only the ch7 row mentions forehead lines), so prompts outside ch7 can lose it.

Hair texture and silhouette: Nagoji's thick, springy curls widen the outline of his head (and as Ananthan Pillai, loose curls still bush out at the sides and nape). Varma's straight hair is combed sleek and flat to the skull, giving a narrow, smooth outline.
Grey: Nagoji has silver-grey streaks at the temples from ch16. Varma's hair is uniformly jet black (sampled temple brightness about 41 for Varma against about 96 for Ananthan Pillai).

Ear ornament: Varma has a large pearl drop hanging below each lobe in a gold setting, a white dot under the ear at 80 px. Nagoji has a small gold stud flush on the lobe, barely visible at 80 px. The bible's Varma line does not specify the pearls either.
Knot position: the Ananthan Pillai topknot sits high on the crown and shows above the forehead in a front view. Varma's knot sits low behind his left ear and barely shows from the front.
Moustache weight: Nagoji's is thick, bushy and wide, covering the lip corners. Varma's is trimmed and thinner, with fine twirled points. This is a weak cue at 80 px.

Face shape: Nagoji's face is broader and squarer, with heavy, low, straight brows (a scowl) and a fleshier nose tip. Varma's is narrower and longer, with hollow cheeks, finer arched brows, a longer, finer nose and deeper lines at the eyes and mouth. This is a weak cue at 80 px.

Neck (costume): Nagoji wears a silver chain with a disc of office (from ch18). Varma wears several strands of gold beads. This is useful in panels but costume, so it was excluded from the costume-hidden judgment.

prompt_lines.nagoji: Nagoji has a broad, square face with heavy, low, straight brows, a thick bushy black handlebar moustache, a bare forehead with no mark, a small gold stud flush on each earlobe with nothing hanging, and thick springy curly black hair that bushes out wide around his head (as Ananthan Pillai gathered into a loose topknot high on the crown, with silver-grey streaks at the temples from chapter 16), never sleek hair, never a side knot, never pearls.
prompt_lines.varma: Marthanda Varma has a narrower, longer, hollow-cheeked face with finer arched brows and lines at the eyes, a neatly trimmed moustache thinner than Nagoji's with fine twirled points, a white Vaishnavite namam with a red centre line from brow to hairline, a large pearl drop hanging below each earlobe, and straight jet-black hair combed sleek and flat to the skull into a small smooth knot low behind his left ear, with no grey anywhere, no curls and never a knot on the crown.

distinctness.verdict: Confusable, mainly from ch16 to ch17 onward. Commander Nagoji (loose curly mane, rust-red turban) against Varma is safe on silhouette alone. Ananthan Pillai against bare-headed Varma in beach, war hall and private scenes is a near double once costume is set aside. The two men share one face type at 80 px: moustached, tan, strong-jawed, clean-chinned and muscular. Both wear their hair tied up and go bare-chested in cream. The face crops with hair, ears and forehead masked were effectively interchangeable, in colour and in greyscale. Telling them apart depends on five add-on cues: Varma's namam, his pearl drops, his sleek jet-black hair, his knot behind the left ear rather than on the crown, and Nagoji's grey temples and curly volume. These are exactly the cues the generator has been dropping or swapping when it draws Varma with grey temples, a crown topknot and Nagoji's heavy moustache. Two gaps in CONTINUITY.md explain some of the drift. First, the Varma base line names none of the namam, the pearl drops or the straight black hair (the namam appears only in the ch7 row). Second, the Ananthan Pillai sheet's build is heavier than the bible's 'lean cavalryman', so the bodies match as well. Adding the namam, the pearl drops and 'straight jet-black hair, no grey' to Varma's base line, and pushing Nagoji leaner and rangier, would be CONTINUITY changes that need the author's approval. I made no project edits.
